metadata.dayBook: Implemented posted-journal-only Day Book projection. It is read-only, preserves full vouchers for account/dimension filtering, excludes cancelled documents by default, separates drafts, supports source/audit drill-down and exports through src/daybook-export.js. Its header, analytic cards, register and sticky balance validation use one invoice-style white report surface; the old voucher/read-time/auto-refresh caption is absent. See docs/DAY-BOOK.md and tests/daybook.test.mjs.
metadata.balanceSheet: Implemented read-only Balance Sheet over posted journal balances through the selected date and branch. It classifies assets, liabilities, equity and current earnings, retains Chart of Accounts drill-down, and presents an expandable accounting hierarchy with debit, credit and positive business-facing closing balances in the Day Book white report surface. See docs/BALANCE-SHEET.md and tests/balance-sheet.test.mjs.

metadata.creditNoteFlow: The Credit Note create page is six sections in flow order: Credit note details (number generated and READ-ONLY, date, type, customer, reason, reason detail, reference), Original invoice details (the picker, then the invoice snapshot as one Invoice INV-0001 link - button.cnInvoiceLink - that opens a right-side popup drawer portalled to window.document.body: div.cnInvoiceLayer (position:fixed, inset:0, right-aligned) holding button.cnInvoiceBackdrop and div.cnInvoiceDrawer (role=dialog, aria-modal, width:min(430px,94vw) folding to 100% below 560px) with a pinned head, one scrolling div.cnInvoiceDrawerBody and the same thirteen read-only facts; the backdrop, the close button and Escape dismiss it, and the open state is the invoice id itself so changing the invoice closes it. It is a div and never an aside, because src/styles.css still hides every aside below 700px with transform:translateX(-100%)), Credit items, Tax summary, Accounting preview, and a collapsed Additional details (customer note, internal note, attachments). The customer is chosen before the invoice and only that customer posted invoices are offered. The items table loads from the invoice - Item, Description, Original quantity, Previously credited, Available quantity, Credit quantity, Unit, Rate, Discount, Tax, Amount, remove - with the credit quantity capped at the available quantity and no per-row invoice-item picker, because the rows ARE the invoice items; tax is inherited and has no control. The note also stores creditMethod (Item Based Credit / Amount Based Credit, normalised through creditMethod()), inventoryImpact (Return Stock To Inventory / Financial Adjustment Only, normalised through inventoryImpact()), adjustmentAmount / adjustmentTax / adjustmentAccount for the value-only path, and companyId / companyName / branchId / branchName for the posting scope. An Amount Based Credit note has no quantities: calculateCredit builds one synthetic line with invoiceItemIndex:-1, takes its tax from the invoice's own blended component rates (billedTaxRates) or from chosenTaxRates(form,taxPolicy) on a standalone note, and caps the credit in total per tax component; it never raises a Sales Return. The create page carries a head status badge, a customer strip stating Net receivable with Available credit, a read-only Organisation / Branch strip, an explicit Inventory impact decision on item-based notes, an Original invoice details card leading with seven read-only facts above the link to the full right-side popup, a Total tax line in the credit summary (the create page shows NO Tax summary card and NO Accounting Impact Preview - both were removed on 2026-09-26 and the posting preview lives on the detail page's Accounting tab), and an Adjustment card stating Adjustment amount, Tax treatment, Place of supply and Adjustment account four to a line. Without Invoice is now Standalone Credit Note, with the old label read through noteType. creditPostingPlan(s,note,totals) in src/credit-note-service.js is the one ordered account plan that both the Accounting Preview and issue() use, and it now honours a note's own adjustmentAccount ahead of the configured mapping; creditNoteStatus answers Approved for an approved but unposted note. The register states Date, Credit note id, Reference, Customer name, Invoice, Status, Amount, Balance and Actions, with nine widths totalling 100 percent, and its row action is one canonical 3-dot menu holding exactly Edit, Preview, Duplicate and Delete (Edit for drafts only, Delete being the module cancellation that reverses a posted note, Duplicate opening a fresh draft); the lifecycle steps and the refund stay on the detail page and the Applications tab. The Account mapping dialog offers both revenue routes: the shared Sales Adjustment Account plus the reason-specific Sales Return, Tax Adjustment and Other Adjustment accounts, each blank meaning inherit; only Sales Adjustment and Accounts Receivable are required, and Inventory Asset and Stock Adjustment are optional because they matter only when a goods return moves stock. The items grid is the shared ivLineTable with soItemCell and ivQtyCell, the unit is the read-only soUnitValue, the add action is the details.soAddItem menu, and the figures close in the shared section.ivCard.soBillingSummary (soSummaryGrid, soCurrencyChip INR, soSummaryMoney with summary(totals), soPostingNote). The page wears the sales-document style: every card is an ivCard soFormSection with a soSectionHead heading, field rows are ivFields soFieldRow, and it opens with the Customer card (soCustomerRow with the shared CustomerSearch, then the soCustomerProfile strip with its Net receivable) exactly as Create Sales Order and Create Sales Invoice do; CustomerSearch and customerInitials are exported from src/SalesDocumentFields.jsx for that reuse.
metadata.documentPreviewSheet: A printed document owns its table geometry, because a preview mounts INSIDE a register page and the host rules reach the sheet: src/document-preview-fix.css restates .dpPaper table{min-width:0}, the sheet th/td padding (10px 6px and 12px 6px, 12px 6px and 14px 6px for .dpItemsTable), a 6px first-child left inset and a 6px last-child right inset under !important, against .itemsPage table{min-width:800px} in src/items.css and the global th/td{padding:16px 20px!important} plus 24px first/last inset in src/ui-system.css. Before 2026-09-26 the eight-column items table measured 800px inside a 620px paper and printed 150px past the right page edge with two-word headers wrapped. The eight .dpItemsTable columns are 4/21/13/12/12/12/10/16 percent and total 100, so the table always equals the paper content box; never give the sheet table a min-width and never add a column without restating every positional width.
metadata.workingContextSwitcher: The portalled dropdown directly provides checkbox multi-selection for organisations and branches with Cancel and Apply. metadata.journalDetail: The Journal detail is ONE section, not four tabs. div.je-detail-single is a minmax(0,7fr) minmax(0,3fr) grid: the left column (div.je-detail-main) holds section.je-detail-facts (heading Journal details) over the field list, details.je-impact (heading View Accounting Impact, closed by default) wrapping the debit and credit table, and section.je-detail-docs (heading Supporting Documents) over the source row and attachments; the right column is div.je-detail-audit (heading Audit Trail, sticky at 12px). The columns stack to one column at 1050px. There is no tab row and no detailTab state. The audit column must be a div, never an aside, because src/styles.css styles every aside as the fixed navigation drawer and would remove it from the grid. A Draft journal shows Submit for approval and a Pending Approval journal shows Publish journal, both primary; the action key stays Approve, the status stays Approved, and ACTION_LABELS holds the label. The field list runs four to a line with an icon on every label and folds to three at 1280px, two at 1050px and one at 700px; section.je-detail-docs (Supporting Documents) lives INSIDE section.je-detail-facts, so one card holds the fields, the source row and the attachments, the accounting-impact accordion closes the column and the audit log keeps the right 30%. A Pending Approval journal renders div.je-permission-note for a role that may not post it, naming the View as switch, so the publish action is never silently absent.

metadata.journalTransactions: Updated 2026-09-24: Journal Entries is transaction-first. The create/edit page is src/SimpleTransactionForm.jsx (Record Transaction) with a Transaction type dropdown (Expense, Income, Transfer, Customer Payment, Vendor Payment), Transaction name, Date, the type's own money fields, Amount, Organisation and Branch, and a collapsed Additional details section (Description, Reference number, attachments). Pay From/Category, Deposit To/Category, From Account/To Account, Customer/optional Invoice/Deposit To and Vendor/optional Bill/Pay From are revealed one type at a time, and a settlement states the document number, date, total and open balance. Debit, Credit and journal-line vocabulary never appear in the normal journey; the double entry lives behind the collapsed View accounting entry block. The lifecycle is Draft -> Pending Approval -> Approved, Pending Approval -> Rejected, Rejected -> Resubmit, Approved -> Reversed and Pending Approval -> Cancelled; only Draft and Rejected are editable, rejection stores a reason and who rejected it, and publishing posts through src/invoice-engine.js journal() with the Journal Transaction source and one idempotent journal-transaction token per record. A payment against an invoice or bill is settled by invoiceCommand('pay') or recordPurchasePayment() and never by a second journal. src/JournalEntriesPro.jsx owns one action() for every transition and derives the acting role from the View as switch, so Publish, Reject and Reverse are removed from the row menu for a role that may not approve. The register shows Journal ID, Date, Transaction Name, Account, Transaction Type, Amount, Status, Organisation, Branch and Actions with no debit or credit column; search covers journal id, transaction name and reference and the filter panel covers status, type, account, organisation, branch and date. src/journal-register-display.js projects those cells for simple and advanced rows without mutating stored records and maps the earlier vocabulary (Pending Approval / Approved -> Pending, Posted -> Published) on read. src/demo-data.js seeds the register so every status and type is represented. The register's third column is Transaction details - the transaction name with its reference stacked beneath it, reading "No reference" when none was recorded - not Transaction name. On the Record Transaction page the entry mode is one Simple / Advanced ModeToggle exported by src/SimpleTransactionForm.jsx and rendered by both editors, the Wayvida will record card was removed at the user's request - the fields run four to a line in one full-width card and the page ends in a footer holding the one-line summary, a View accounting entry tooltip and the Cancel, Save draft, Submit for approval and Publish now actions, which pin to the window while the page scrolls; Description, Reference number and the attachment control share one row of Additional details, and the Transaction type dropdown opens with Expense selected and no empty option. The register shows ten transactions to a view behind the shared .pagination-footer pager and keeps a 24px first and last cell inset so the list has a left and right gutter inside its card. Browser-local persistence and the role simulation remain prototype constraints.

metadata.salesOrdersRegister: Sales orders register columns (2026-09-25): the register is EIGHT columns - Order (the SO number over its order date through fmtDate), Customer, Organisation, Branch, Amount, Status, Payment status, Actions - at 12/15/17/12/11/10/11/12 percent, and soOrdersTable widths are positional so any column change means restating all eight. Organisation and Branch are cells of their own in that order, matching the invoices register, and they replaced the single Branch & Organisation cell that printed the branch over the organisation. There is NO Created by column, removed on the user request of 2026-09-25; Created by survives as a register FILTER, the same choice made for the invoices Order ID, because removing a column is not the same as removing the ability to search by it. src/sales-orders.css must keep exactly ONE run of those eight width rules - it used to carry two identical runs, the first entirely overridden by the second, and the dead one has been deleted. Status and Payment status still render the shared StatusPill through ORDER_TONES and PAYMENT_TONES, and every row still ends in the 36x36 button.soRowIconButton eye that opens the order preview plus the row action menu.
metadata.invoiceRegister: Invoice register, detail actions and the row-action eyes (2026-09-25): the Sales invoices register is EIGHT fixed columns - Invoice, Customer, Status, Invoice amount, Payment status, Organisation, Branch, Actions - at 13/16/11/12/12/16/11/9 percent, and because .ivInvoiceTable widths are positional any column change means restating all eight; the credit-note register overrides all eight for its own table. There is NO Order ID column, because the order reference is read on the invoice detail page (the stats row states Order number and status and the details list states Reference), so orderNumberOf(i) survives only as the register Order ID FILTER; and the lifecycle Status sits AHEAD of the amount by the user request of 2026-09-25, which also puts the amount back in the fourth column so its existing td:nth-child(4) right-align rule still covers it. Organisation and Branch are cells of their own rather than one merged cell, and the invoice number cell carries {i.date} alone - the raw stored status used to sit there and would print Draft beside a Status column reading Pending. The Status cell is StatusPill status={invoiceDisplayStatus(i)} tone={invoiceDisplayTone(i)} from src/invoice-register-display.js, the one display rule: Cancelled wins first, then posted means Published, then Pending Approval means Pending, else Draft. It is presentation only and never rewrites a stored status, so Paid, Sent, Partially Paid and Overdue all read Published while a cancelled invoice that once posted stays Cancelled. The row action is button.ivIconButton, a 36x36 square holding IconEye with aria-label={'View '+i.number}, matching the row-menu trigger beside it. On the Sales orders register the row action is button.soRowIconButton, a 36x36 eye whose aria-label reads Preview <number> and which calls setPrintDoc(x) to open DocumentPreview for that order, whether or not it has an invoice; the invoice hand-off moved into the row menu through a new onOpenInvoice prop, whose invoice entry is disabled only when there is no invoice AND the order is not Confirmed, opening the invoice when one exists and converting only when it does not, so invoiceIdOf and the wayvida-open-invoice handshake stay in use. On the invoice detail screen a Draft offers Edit with its icon beside a primary Submit for approval, and on the create page div.soBarActions carries Cancel, Save draft and Submit for approval through one saveInvoice(status) saver: Save draft is the form submit button and takes the primary fill only when invoiceAllowed(role,'submit') is false, so the page always has exactly one primary action, and a refused submit leaves the form bound to the saved record so a retry edits it rather than creating a second invoice. The create page never posts.
metadata.numberCurrencyFormat: Number and Currency Format (2026-09-25): ONE module, src/number-format.js, decides how every figure in the app is written. It reads and writes its preference through src/settings-store.js (numberFormat, currencySymbol, roundOffQuantity, roundOffRate and the existing decimalPlaces, all under organization) and exports formatRupees(value,override) for rupee values, formatMinor(minor,override) for the engine stored paise, formatQuantity and formatRate for the two round-off switches, numberSample, decimalChoiceOf, digitsOfChoice, saveNumberFormat and useNumberFormat(). Every money helper in the app delegates to it - the engine money plus the file-local helpers in Customers.jsx, GeneralLedgerPro.jsx, SalesOrderActions.jsx, SalesOrders.jsx, Vendors.jsx, simple-journal-transaction.js, journal-templates.js, inventory-adjustments.js and Items.jsx - so no en-IN currency literal remains on a money surface; item prices are rupees and engine amounts are paise, so never hand one to the other formatter. src/NumberCurrencyFormatDialog.jsx renders NumberFormatControl, a 40px button.soHeadSettings in the LIGHT primary variant because the one solid primary fill on the create page is Save, mounted by BOTH create hosts inside .soCreateHead. The dialog is a .nfLayer fixed layer copying the address editor layer, backdrop, card, close-button and footer tokens, offering the two number systems with their own samples, a country list, six decimal-digit choices (Default IS two decimals, which is why decimalChoiceOf(2) returns default), the two round-off switches, a custom symbol and a live preview. Its label rules are scoped .nfLayer .nfFormat / .nfLayer .nfDigits label because .invoiceWorkspace label outranks a bare single-class selector and otherwise stacks and centres the radios. Round-off moves quantities and rates only, never a posted amount.
metadata.salesDocumentCreate: Create Sales Order and the New sales invoice page render ONE shared component, src/SalesDocumentFields.jsx, as ONE STACKED COLUMN with no second column and no rail: the document details, the customer, the lines and the Billing summary, in that order, each the full width of the page. The details card leads and its header row is FOUR fields on one row (.soFieldRow4) - the document ID, the document date, the Reference number and the Payment terms - with the scope pair (.soFieldRow2) holding Organisation and Branch on the row beneath, which is the order the user specified on 2026-09-25. The ID field is editable and states the number the save will take as its PLACEHOLDER (placeholder={autoNumber||"Automatic"}), fed by autoNumber: the host pages pass nextSalesOrderNumber(orders) from src/sales-order-service.js and nextInvoiceNumber(db.invoices) from src/invoice-engine.js, which are the same functions saveSalesOrder and command("save") now call, so the number shown and the number assigned can never be two implementations. Never put a new document number in value: a value taken at form-open can be taken by another operator before the save, where a placeholder cannot. Every field is the Record Transaction control the journal create page uses: function Field({label,icon:Icon,hint,children}) renders label.soField over span.soControl, with an 18px stroke={1.8} icon inside the control and the input or select transparent within it. The marks are IconHash (document ID), IconCalendar (date), IconFileText (reference), IconClock (payment terms), IconBuildingBank (organisation), IconSitemap (branch), IconUser (customer) and IconMapPin (place of supply). The tokens are restated under .soCreatePage in src/sales-orders.css rather than borrowed from record-transaction.css, so each page sheet stays self-contained. The customer field is a PLAIN SEARCH BOX, not the shared SearchSelect combobox: CustomerSearch owns an input with role="combobox", a div.soCustomerResults listbox under it, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Enter/Escape and an outside-pointer dismissal, filtering the active customers by name, code, phone and GSTIN. Two rules are load-bearing: focus must clear the query and reopen the list (onFocus sets open true, query empty and active 0), and choosing must release the caret (inputRef.current.blur() inside pick). Without both, the box keeps the committed name on screen with the input still focused, so the next search appends to that name instead of starting over. The root is a div, never a label, because an option row inside a label re-fires the field it labels. The chosen customer reads in div.soCustomerProfile: a 52px profile column holding span.soCustomerAvatar (the customer initials from customerInitials()) beside dl.soCustomerFacts, which is TWO columns with the billing address spanning a full row through .soCustomerFactWide{grid-column:1/-1} and Phone and GSTIN side by side beneath it. The address prints through addressLines(which) as separate lines - street, city and state, PIN and country - because the document already stores it structured. The rest of the master data stays behind details.soCustomerMore (View customer details), closed by default. Place of supply is NOT on the details card: the two host pages render the exported PlaceOfSupplyField from src/SalesDocumentFields.jsx inside their Additional details block, which recomputes its own source line and reset. Both pages therefore carry open={!form.place} on details.soMoreCard, because calculate() refuses to total anything without a place of supply and a required field must never be stranded inside a closed disclosure. The three place helpers were hoisted to module scope for that: placeIsManual, placeSuggestionOf and applyPlaceFor. The old soAdvancedAccounting disclosure and its five rules are deleted, along with the dead .soCustomerSummary rules and the soFactItemWide span rules. The shipment, delivery and salesperson fields were REMOVED from the create page at the user request, with their Shipment group. Known leftover: the Sales Orders register still exposes an Expected shipment from/to filter over order.shipment, which nothing can now set, so it can never match; it was left in place because removing a register filter is a separate behavioural change, and should either be removed or the field restored. The Billing summary is the last card: section.ivCard.soBillingSummary holds div.soSummaryHead with the heading alone, then div.soSummaryMoney - a right-aligned column whose FIRST child is span.soCurrencyChip reading INR with the rupee sign and whose second is the ivTotals panel - and then p.soPostingNote. The chip sits directly above the Subtotal row at the user request, not beside the heading. The lines heading carries span.soItemsCount with the live line count. The sales line grid is SIX columns and SEVEN cells: Item, Quantity (the unit inside div.ivQtyCell - a read-only span.soUnitValue on an order, input.soUnitInput on an invoice), Rate with the rupee sign and small.ivPriceType under it, Discount, Tax, Amount and the remove action. Widths are 26/13/12/15/20/10 per cent plus a fixed width:46px action column. The cell padding is .soCreatePage .ivLineTable th,.soCreatePage .ivLineTable td{padding:10px 8px!important;height:auto!important;overflow:hidden} and the !important is load-bearing: src/ui-system.css closes with a global table block pinning every td to padding:16px 20px !important;height:64px, which was padding this grid 40px a cell and truncating the tax and amount columns. + Add item is details.soAddItem (an existing item, an ad hoc line via addLine("adHoc"), and Create a new item through ITEM_CREATE_KEY from src/quick-create.js, which src/Items.jsx reads once on mount and clears). Additional details is one section.soMoreGroup per job, and the per-line tax states one rate, "GST <rate>%", with the component split kept inside its menu. The chosen customer reads in ONE compact flex strip capped at 80px (div.soCustomerProfile: display:flex;align-items:center;gap:16px;max-height:80px;overflow:hidden) - a 44px soCustomerAvatar, the name, then dl.soCustomerFacts running Billing, Phone and GSTIN along one baseline - replacing a two-row grid that made the Customer card about 486px tall for three short facts. Measured live at 1440px the strip is 66px and the card 273px. The address prints on one line through addressLine(which), which prints each part once because a stored address can repeat itself (the seed carries city:"India" beside country:"India"), with the full value in the title; it is the only part that shrinks (.soCustomerFact is flex:none so Phone and GSTIN keep their width, .soCustomerFactWide is flex:1 1 0). Below 900px the strip keeps the same single line and the same 80px ceiling and drops the address, which stays in the View customer details disclosure. Do not restore the grid or lift the cap. The create page order is Customer first, then the details card, then the lines, then the Billing summary, switched back on 2026-09-25 at the user request. The customer card names itself once: h3 Customer * carries the label and the required mark, and the search field below has no visible label of its own. The details scope row is THREE fields (.soFieldRow3): Organisation, Branch and Place of supply, with PlaceOfSupplyField rendered by src/SalesDocumentFields.jsx itself, so Additional details lost its Tax block and its open={!form.place} and holds Terms, History and Documents only. The Billing summary is an invoice-style footer: div.soSummaryGrid is minmax(0,1fr) minmax(300px,400px) with the Customer note textarea on the left and soSummaryMoney (currency chip, totals, posting note) on the right, stacking below 900px; the note is the document own form.notes and the Additional-details Customer-notes control was deleted rather than duplicated. The + Add item control is the light primary variant (border 1px solid #bcd0f5, background #eef4ff, color #245fd9) so the solid fill belongs only to Save and confirm. The customer card ends in its own actions, with .soCustomerMore a flex column at align-items:flex-end. The customer strip holds TWO bold lines and nothing else - strong.soCustomerName then span.soCustomerAddress reading "Billing Address:" plus the whole address - keeping the same 80px ceiling (measured 66px); the separate soCustomerFacts strip was removed and the rest of the record is behind View customer details. addressLine(which) is the only address formatter: it prints line1, line2, city, state, pin de-duplicated, drops any part equal to the country and appends the country once, because a stored record can hold the country in its city field. The pen (details.soFactEdit) and button.soCustomerMoreToggle share ONE row at the card trailing edge in div.soCustomerActions; the disclosure is a button with aria-expanded rather than a native details, because a details cannot put its summary and its body in two places, and its body is div.soCustomerMoreBody rendered only while open. There is NO Additional details card on either create page: its panels are passed into src/SalesDocumentFields.jsx as children and rendered in the Billing summary left column under the Customer note (the Terms group, the order history and the Documents drop zone), so soMoreCard, soMoreTitle, soMoreBody and soMoreHint are deleted and form.notes and form.termsAndConditions each have exactly one control. The summary is the invoice arrangement: div.soSummaryGrid is minmax(0,1fr) minmax(300px,400px) with div.soSummaryLeft (Customer note then children) and div.soSummaryRight (the Billing summary heading, the INR chip, the totals and the posting note), so the heading sits directly above the figures. Card padding is 14px 16px, the gap between cards 12px and the section-heading gap 10px. Since 2026-09-25 the card's two actions are ICON-ONLY - a 34x34 aria-label="Edit address" pencil and a 34x34 aria-label="View customer details" eye button - and div.soCustomerRef is a two-column grid (minmax(0,1fr) auto, align-items:center, gap 10px) so they share the strip row at the trailing edge, with div.soCustomerMoreBody, p.soCreditNotice and the empty state spanning both columns through grid-column:1/-1. .soCustomerProfile therefore sits at margin-top:0 (a grid does not collapse a first child top margin) and .soCustomerActions at margin-top:0, which took the card from 220px to 178px at 1440px. .soCustomerAddress is #475467/12.5px/400 with a 600-weight Billing Address label, so the address is a caption under the 14px/650 name. div.soSummaryGrid is now minmax(0,50fr) minmax(0,35fr) with justify-content:space-between - 631px left and 442px right of a 1093px grid with a 20px gap - and the INR chip stays right-aligned to its column while the heading starts at the column start.Since 2026-09-25 the customer row is display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px with .soCustomerRow>.soFieldSearch{flex:0 1 640px} and a 40x40 aria-label="Create customer" IconPlus button at its end, which stashes the draft, sets the one-shot CUSTOMER_CREATE_KEY (wayvida-open-customer-create) and returns through wayvida-return-to so src/Customers.jsx opens a blank form and the draft comes back; The register carries nine columns - Journal ID, Date, Transaction Name, Account, Transaction Type, Amount, Status, Organisation, Branch and Actions - with no Debit or Credit column, and its amount is the user-facing transaction amount. Status is Draft, Pending, Published, Rejected or Reversed; only Draft and Rejected are editable, and a Published transaction is corrected solely by its reversal, which keeps the original posting and its audit trail. One action() in src/JournalEntriesPro.jsx performs every transition: Draft/Rejected save and resubmit, Pending publishes or rejects with a reason, Published reverses. saveSimple() posts through src/invoice-engine.js journal() with the Journal Transaction source and one idempotent journal-transaction token per record, so editing, duplicating or retrying can never double-post; a payment against an invoice or bill is delegated to invoiceCommand('pay') or recordPurchasePayment(), which own the receivable/payable posting and the document balance. The acting role follows the View as switch (the same local simulation src/inventory-adjustments.js uses) and journalAllowed() owns the duty table, so Publish, Reject and Reverse are filtered out of the row menu for any role that may not approve. src/simple-journal-transaction.js owns the vocabulary, validation, plain-language summary, posting lines, journal numbering (JE-<financial year>-<six digits>), duplication and the reversal record; src/journal-register-display.js resolves register cells for simple and advanced rows without mutating stored data. Register rows whose lines name an organisation and branch must match the working context, while a row with no scope at all is treated as a legacy posting. Advanced manual journals keep their original editor behind Advanced mode and their statuses normalise into the same vocabulary. No journal validation, posting rule or stored amount unit changed. modules.accountingImpact: 2026-09-18: the Sites worker serves the built client with the existing SPA fallback and hosts the one server-side route the app needs, POST /api/gst/lookup. The route exists in the worker and not in the browser so the GST/GSP credential stays a server secret: it reads GST_API_URL and GST_API_KEY from the worker environment, sends the key upstream in an x-api-key header, maps the provider field names (lgnm / tradeNam / sts / dty / stcd, pradr.addr) onto one taxpayer shape and returns {ok, status, taxpayer, fetchedAt}. It never echoes the credential and never falls through to the asset handler. Failures are machine-readable - 400 invalid_gstin, 503 not_configured, 502 unavailable or upstream_error, 404 not_found, 405 method_not_allowed - so the form can show a clear message and still let the operator type the details. No accounting amount is read or written by this route.
